negative_findings.description: No public, itemised bank-client reference list was found for 4iG, Grepton or Sysdata PSE. Searches in Hungarian returned only generic capability language ('pénzügyi szektor', 'rendszerintegráció') without named bank accounts.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sector positioning confirmed; specific bank names not disclosed on public marketing pages in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Account-level attribution for these integrators will have to come from procurement notices, annual-report customer-concentration notes, job ads and press coverage rather than vendor reference pages.

negative_findings.description: No IBM Hungary press announcement naming a Hungarian bank client (OTP, K&H) for a core-banking or infrastructure project surfaced in en-language search; the OTP core selection that did surface is with Intellect/iGCB, not IBM.
negative_findings.result_summary: IBM Hungary's bank-facing footprint remains unquantified from public search alone.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: IBM Hungary is in the cell's actor list but currently has no verified public evidence base; treat its competitive weight as unknown rather than assumed.

negative_findings.description: 'Sysdata' is ambiguous in Hungary: results resolve to Sysdata PSE Kft. (software engineering, since 1991) rather than a 'Sysdata Zrt.'. 'Docler' likewise did not resolve to any banking-IT entity; the relevant local ISV in the wealth/securities space is Dorsum Zrt.
negative_findings.result_summary: Actor list needs correction: Sysdata PSE Kft. and Dorsum Zrt. are the real entities; 'Docler' appears to be a mis-specification.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Querying wrong legal names produces false negatives and wasted crawl budget; entity resolution against the company registry should precede collection.

negative_findings.description: The CARDNET corporate homepage (https://www.cardnet.hu/) was inferred from the company name and third-party profiles; it was not fetched in this pass, and no direct-fetch verification was performed on any URL in this slice.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded with reduced confidence pending the deterministic liveness pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a plausible-but-wrong domain from entering the source register as verified.

coverage_gaps.description: Several likely local competitors were not yet investigated: Synergon, WSH (rendszerintegracio), Online Üzleti Informatika Zrt., Scriptum, ITSH/Deutsche Telekom Systems Hungary, Nexon, and the Hungarian arms of Accenture/Deloitte that act as bank-side prime consultants.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a second HU pass on these names with 'banki', 'pénzintézet', 'referencia', 'ügyfeleink' and check each against e-beszamolo for revenue scale.

coverage_gaps.description: No job-advertisement source was captured. Hungarian job boards (profession.hu, LinkedIn HU) are a strong indirect signal: integrator postings routinely name the client bank's platform and project.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add profession.hu and LinkedIn HU job-posting monitoring for the actor list, filtered on 'banki', 'core banking', platform names.

coverage_gaps.description: MNB-side sources on bank IT outsourcing (kiszervezési nyilvántartás / outsourcing registers, supervisory inspection reports naming IT suppliers) were not searched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search mnb.hu for 'kiszervezés', 'kiszervezett tevékenységek nyilvántartása' and supervisory decisions (határozat) that name IT service providers to banks.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of the local integrator set is thin — most of these firms publish substantive references only in Hungarian, and only the foreign-vendor announcements were found in English.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat HU as the primary collection language for this cell; use EN only for foreign-vendor and group-level (Magyar Telekom, IBM, KBC) announcements.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add Wayback Machine snapshots of the vendors' 'referenciák' / 'ügyfeleink' pages to recover deleted client lists.

brief: The Hungarian bank-IT competitive set splits into three tiers of source: listed or group-backed primes (4iG, T-Systems Magyarország) whose regulated disclosures and press rooms are rich and reliable; specialist domestic ISVs and payment operators (Dorsum, CARDNET, NETLOCK, Integra, Mindspire) whose own blogs and product pages occasionally name bank clients outright; and mid-size integrators (Grepton, Sysdata PSE) that publish capability language but no bank references at all. Because vendor reference lists are largely absent, the highest-value sources for this cell are structural rather than promotional: the Közbeszerzési Adatbázis/EKR procurement registry and the e-beszamolo statutory accounts portal, which together attribute contracts and size the banking revenue behind the marketing. Trade press (Bitport, HWSW, ITBusiness) and the annual Portfolio Banking Technology programme supply the connective tissue — win/loss stories and a yearly census of who is actively selling to Hungarian banks. Collection must be Hungarian-first; note that 'Sysdata' resolves to Sysdata PSE Kft. and the intended local wealth-management ISV is Dorsum Zrt., not Docler.
